## Remediation and Account Restriction Actions

Remediation of the Summit Gate Produce Enterprises LLC relationship commenced immediately following the identification of the anomalous outbound wire transfer. The investigating analyst placed a firm hold on account 57-14456-1 on August 21, 2023, pending contact with the customer and the recovery of funds. This hold restricted all outbound transactions, including automated clearing house debits, wire transfers, and internal book transfers, while permitting incoming deposits to credit the account.

The relationship manager was notified of the restriction and directed to contact Beatriz Underhill to establish whether the $431,944.09 wire transfer to Fieldstone Exports Holdings Ltd. was authorized and, if authorized, whether the payment instructions had been verified against known vendor records. The relationship manager reported that Underhill confirmed she had authorized the wire transfer, believing it to be a valid payment for an outstanding invoice from Anvil Equipment Holdings Ltd. Underhill stated she had received an email from an individual purporting to be an Anvil Equipment Holdings Ltd. accounts receivable representative, instructing her to remit payment to the Fieldstone Exports Holdings Ltd. account at the receiving institution.

Upon receipt of this information, the reviewing analyst determined that the activity was consistent with a business email compromise scheme. Cortex Bank and Trust immediately initiated a recall request for the $431,944.09 wire transfer with the receiving institution. A hold-harmless agreement was executed and transmitted to the receiving institution to facilitate the return of funds. The receiving institution confirmed receipt of the recall request and placed a freeze on the beneficiary account.

The receiving institution subsequently reported that the beneficiary account had been largely depleted prior to the imposition of the freeze. A sum of $73,430.50 was recovered and returned to Cortex Bank and Trust account 57-14456-1. The residual loss to Summit Gate Produce Enterprises LLC in this matter is $358,513.59. Cortex Bank and Trust considers the recovery effort concluded.

Following the initial containment actions and the partial recovery of funds, Cortex Bank and Trust conducted a review of the Summit Gate Produce Enterprises LLC relationship to determine appropriate ongoing controls. The review considered the nature of the compromise, the customer's response, and the potential for future risk. It was determined that the customer's email infrastructure had likely been compromised, allowing the threat actor to monitor communications and insert fraudulent payment instructions. The threat actor utilized a lookalike sender domain differing by one character from the legitimate Anvil Equipment Holdings Ltd. domain, a tactic frequently observed in business email compromise schemes. The fraudulent email also employed urgency language, which contributed to the customer bypassing internal dual-approval controls and initiating the funds transfer minutes before the wire cutoff.

Based on these findings, Cortex Bank and Trust implemented a series of enhanced security measures for the Summit Gate Produce Enterprises LLC relationship. The customer's access to the online wire initiation module was revoked. All future wire transfers must be initiated via written request submitted to a Cortex Bank and Trust branch and require in-person verification by an authorized signer on the account. This restriction mitigates the risk of unauthorized wire transfers originating from compromised online banking credentials or fraudulent email instructions.

In addition to the channel limitation, account 57-14456-1 was placed under enhanced monitoring. A custom monitoring rule was configured to generate an alert for any outbound transaction exceeding a threshold, regardless of the transaction channel. This threshold was established based on the historical transaction profile of the account and the typical value of payments made to legitimate vendors. The enhanced monitoring rule requires the relationship manager to contact the customer and verify the transaction details prior to release.

The relationship manager also conducted a security awareness discussion with Beatriz Underhill, emphasizing the importance of verifying payment instructions through secondary channels, such as a phone call to a known contact at the vendor, prior to initiating funds transfers. Underhill was advised to implement robust internal controls, including mandatory dual-approval for all outbound payments, and to conduct regular cybersecurity training for employees responsible for financial transactions. Underhill confirmed that Summit Gate Produce Enterprises LLC had engaged a third-party cybersecurity firm to investigate the email compromise and implement remediation measures.

Cortex Bank and Trust also reviewed the activity of Lakebridge Industrial Supply LLC, account 79-44138-3, which shares common ownership with Summit Gate Produce Enterprises LLC. A review of account 79-44138-3 for the period July 27, 2023 through August 30, 2023 identified no activity indicative of a business email compromise or unauthorized funds transfers. However, out of an abundance of caution, the online wire initiation module for account 79-44138-3 was temporarily suspended pending confirmation from the customer that their email infrastructure had been secured.

The reviewing analyst conducted a review of the counterparties identified in this matter. A search of Cortex Bank and Trust records determined that Fieldstone Exports Holdings Ltd., Cardinal Trading Holdings Ltd., Crescent Exports Partners LP, and Hearthstone Management Holdings Ltd. do not maintain accounts with the institution. No further action can be taken regarding these entities.

The Summit Gate Produce Enterprises LLC relationship will remain under enhanced monitoring for a period of one year. The relationship manager will maintain regular contact with the customer to monitor the implementation of internal security controls and to assess the ongoing risk posed by the relationship. Cortex Bank and Trust will continue to monitor the account for suspicious activity and file subsequent reports as required by regulatory obligations. The decision to maintain the relationship was based on the customer's cooperation during the investigation, their commitment to improving internal security controls, and the absence of evidence suggesting complicity in the fraudulent activity. The receiving institution confirmed receipt of the wire transfer and indicated that the beneficiary name on the account did not match the name of the invoicing vendor provided by Beatriz Underhill. The receiving institution disclosed that the account belonged to Cardinal Trading Holdings Ltd. The receiving institution further advised that a portion of the funds had already been disbursed prior to their receipt of the recall request from Cortex Bank and Trust. The receiving institution confirmed that a hold had been placed on the remaining balance in the beneficiary account. The amount successfully frozen by the receiving institution was $73,430.50. The bank requested that the receiving institution return the frozen funds; however, the receiving institution stated that they required a hold harmless agreement and formal indemnification before releasing the funds. Cortex Bank and Trust initiated the necessary legal processes to secure the return of the frozen amount. The information obtained through the 314(b) request confirmed that the funds had been directed to an unintended beneficiary and that a significant portion of the transfer had been irretrievably lost.

Following the initial 314(b) exchange, Cortex Bank and Trust engaged in further communication with the receiving institution to coordinate the recovery effort. The bank provided the receiving institution with a detailed summary of the events leading up to the wire transfer, including the deceptive email communication and the customer's belief that she was paying a legitimate invoice. The receiving institution acknowledged the information but maintained their requirement for formal indemnification before releasing the frozen funds. Cortex Bank and Trust continued to monitor the status of the frozen funds and maintained contact with the receiving institution's fraud department. The bank's legal counsel reviewed the hold harmless agreement provided by the receiving institution. The process of recovering the frozen funds remained ongoing at the conclusion of the review period. The bank recorded the residual loss to the customer as $358,513.59, representing the difference between the initial wire amount and the funds successfully frozen at the receiving institution.

On August 30, 2023, the bank received a supplementary information request from the federal law enforcement agency that had initiated the initial inquiry on August 17, 2023. The agency requested any additional information obtained by the bank subsequent to their initial request, specifically inquiring about the results of any interbank communication or attempts to recover the funds. Cortex Bank and Trust provided a summary of the information obtained through the Section 314(b) exchange with the receiving institution. The bank detailed the confirmation that the beneficiary account name did not match the intended vendor and provided the name of the actual beneficiary, Cardinal Trading Holdings Ltd. The bank also informed the agency of the amount successfully frozen by the receiving institution and the ongoing efforts to secure its return. The bank provided copies of the communication with the receiving institution regarding the hold harmless agreement. The bank continued to cooperate with all law enforcement inquiries and provided updates as new information became available. The bank maintained a record of all requests received and the corresponding information provided to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements and to support any potential investigation into the fraudulent activity. The bank's interaction with law enforcement and other financial institutions focused on documenting the circumstances of the fraud and attempting to mitigate the loss incurred by the customer.

## Filing Determination

Cortex Bank and Trust is filing this report because the activity described above is consistent with funds induced out of a customer account by deception and moved by wire to a beneficiary the customer never intended to pay and no legitimate business purpose was identified for it. The determination rests on the key finding recorded above. The relationship has been placed under enhanced monitoring, the monitoring scenarios that generated the underlying alerts have been retuned for this customer segment, and a relationship review has been scheduled. Supporting documentation is retained in internal case file FIU-2024-1727 and is available to law enforcement on request.

A review of wire transfer records confirmed that $981,952.31 was credited to the account on May 15, 2024, originating from Umberfield Management LLC. body:
## Report Header

Filing institution: Cortex Bank and Trust
Internal case reference: FIU-2024-1728
Report filed: July 2, 2024
Suspected activity: sanctions / OFAC
Risk tier: medium
Subjects of this report:
  Greystone Management Trading Co. (business), account 77-26136-1
  Obsidian Produce Corp. (business), account 32-19231-2
  Marblehead Capital Group LLC (business), account 47-68844-3
Review period: August 11, 2023 through June 14, 2024
Aggregate amount of activity reviewed: $640,768.29

## Activity Overview

This review was initiated following an automated monitoring alert generated on the account of Greystone Management Trading Co. (account 77-26136-1). The alert, triggered during the review period of August 11, 2023, through June 14, 2024, identified a potential match against a Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list maintained by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC). The activity under review involves international wire transfers and trade finance transactions, raising concerns regarding potential exposure to a sanctioned party or jurisdiction. The aggregate value of the screened transactions under review is $640,768.29. The reviewing analyst noted that the transactions were processed through Cortex Bank and Trust's international correspondent banking channels.

The initial alert was generated in response to a payment instruction submitted by Greystone Management Trading Co. on August 11, 2023. The transaction details included a counterparty, Tidewater Logistics Trading Co., with an address that the automated screening system identified as potentially located within a comprehensively sanctioned jurisdiction. Upon review of the transaction, the payment was held pending resolution of the name match. The amount of this held payment was $444,469.39. Subsequent investigation into the counterparty and the associated trade documents revealed anomalies that warranted further scrutiny. The activity is consistent with attempts to obscure the true origin or destination of funds and goods, a typology often associated with sanctions evasion.

Following the initial alert on August 11, 2023, the reviewing analyst examined a subsequent transaction initiated on August 18, 2023. This transaction, a wire transfer, involved a counterparty named Silverthorn Fabrication Inc. A review of the transaction details and accompanying documentation revealed that the shipping documents associated with the underlying trade had been re-routed through a known transshipment hub. This routing appeared inconsistent with the stated origin and destination of the goods, raising further concerns about the potential involvement of sanctioned entities or jurisdictions. The declared value of the shipment named in the trade documents was $504,014.65. The use of transshipment hubs is a recognized method for obfuscating the true path of goods, complicating efforts to ensure compliance with international sanctions.

On August 21, 2023, the automated system flagged another transaction, this time involving Eastbrook Distribution Partners LP. The screening system identified an intermediate owner of Eastbrook Distribution Partners LP who held exactly forty-nine percent of the company's shares. This ownership structure, while not inherently illegal, is frequently observed in attempts to evade the OFAC fifty percent rule, which states that any entity owned fifty percent or more in the aggregate by one or more blocked persons is itself considered blocked. The reviewing analyst noted that this specific ownership percentage warranted enhanced due diligence to determine the true beneficial ownership and control of Eastbrook Distribution Partners LP and its potential connections to sanctioned individuals or entities.

Further review of the account activity on August 24, 2023, revealed a pattern of wire transfers where the payment references appeared to have been stripped of originator detail. This obfuscation tactic is often employed to bypass automated screening filters and conceal the identities of the parties involved in the transaction. The absence of complete and accurate originator information complicates the bank's ability to perform adequate sanctions screening and assess the risk associated with the transactions. The reviewing analyst noted that these transactions involved several counterparties, including Saltmarsh Distribution Partners LP and Ironwood Trading Inc. The lack of transparency in these transactions further heightened concerns regarding potential sanctions evasion.

The investigation expanded to include a review of transactions involving other entities related to the primary subject, Greystone Management Trading Co. On August 28, 2023, a transaction involving Obsidian Produce Corp. (account 32-19231-2) was flagged for review. The transaction details exhibited similarities to the previously identified suspicious activity, including the use of complex routing and the involvement of counterparties with opaque ownership structures. The reviewing analyst noted that the relationship between Greystone Management Trading Co. and Obsidian Produce Corp. required further investigation to determine the nature of their business dealings and the potential for coordinated efforts to circumvent sanctions controls.

On September 13, 2023, a transaction involving Marblehead Capital Group LLC (account 47-68844-3) was also identified for review. This transaction involved a payment instruction that was subsequently blocked and reported to OFAC. The payment blocked and reported amounted to $656,822.37. The reviewing analyst noted that the details of this transaction, including the counterparties involved and the nature of the underlying business, were consistent with the typology of sanctions evasion observed in the other transactions under review. The blocking and reporting of this transaction underscored the seriousness of the potential sanctions violations and the need for a comprehensive investigation into the activities of the subject entities.

The reviewing analyst continued to monitor the account activity throughout September 2023. On September 18, 2023, and September 19, 2023, further transactions involving the subject entities and their counterparties were reviewed. These transactions exhibited similar red flags, including the use of transshipment hubs and the obfuscation of originator details. The pattern of activity suggested a coordinated effort to move funds and goods in a manner that bypassed established sanctions controls. The reviewing analyst noted that the complexity of the transactions and the involvement of multiple entities and jurisdictions presented significant challenges in determining the true nature of the activity.

By September 25, 2023, the reviewing analyst had compiled a substantial body of evidence indicating potential sanctions evasion by the subject entities. The investigation focused on clarifying the relationships between the entities, identifying the true beneficial owners, and determining the ultimate destination of the funds and goods involved in the transactions. The reviewing analyst noted that the activity under review presented a significant risk of exposure to sanctioned parties and jurisdictions and required a thorough and comprehensive investigation to ensure compliance with applicable regulations and laws. The findings of this investigation will be detailed in the subsequent sections of this report.

## Subject Background and Relationship History

Obsidian Produce Corp. established its relationship with Cortex Bank and Trust on August 11, 2023, opening commercial operating account 32-19231-2. At onboarding, the customer was assigned a medium risk rating, consistent with its declared business model in wholesale agricultural commodities. The customer profile indicated expected activity primarily consisting of domestic wire transfers and automated clearing house payments, with occasional international wires related to seasonal sourcing. The relationship manager noted the business structure was complex, with an intermediate owner holding exactly forty-nine percent, a detail that was documented but did not initially elevate the risk rating beyond the medium tier. The primary account signatories were documented as US residents, and the physical address provided was a commercial office suite.

The initial review of account activity against the expected profile revealed significant deviations. While the customer had anticipated primarily domestic activity, the observed transaction flow was heavily weighted toward international wire transfers, a pattern not aligned with the stated business model. The aggregate value of the screened transactions under review, $640,768.29, was largely comprised of these international wires. The volume and velocity of these transactions were inconsistent with the seasonal sourcing described at onboarding. The reviewing analyst noted that the account appeared to function less as an operating account for a domestic produce wholesaler and more as a conduit for international funds transfers.

Further analysis of the counterparty data associated with these international wires identified Tidewater Logistics Trading Co. as a frequent beneficiary. The volume of funds remitted to Tidewater Logistics Trading Co. was disproportionate to the declared size and scope of Obsidian Produce Corp.'s operations. The relationship manager attempted to clarify the nature of these payments, but the customer was unable to substantiate the business purpose for the high volume of international remittances to this specific counterparty. The customer's explanations regarding supply chain disruptions and the need for alternative sourcing did not adequately account for the transactional behavior observed in the account.

The review also identified several transactions involving Silverthorn Fabrication Inc., a counterparty that did not appear to have a clear connection to the wholesale agricultural commodities sector. The payments to Silverthorn Fabrication Inc. were characterized by vague payment references, often stripped of originator detail, a pattern that hindered efforts to fully understand the economic purpose of the transfers. The reviewing analyst considered the possibility that Obsidian Produce Corp. was operating outside its declared line of business, potentially acting as a payment processor or intermediary for third parties. The customer's inability to provide satisfactory documentation for these transactions further complicated the assessment of the account's risk profile.

A subsequent review of trade documents associated with certain international wires raised additional concerns. The shipping documents provided by Obsidian Produce Corp. indicated that goods were frequently re-routed through a transshipment hub, a practice that, while not inherently illicit, adds complexity to the supply chain and can obscure the ultimate origin or destination of the goods. The declared value of the shipment named in the trade documents, $504,014.65, was substantial, and the routing through a transshipment hub appeared inconsistent with the direct sourcing model described at onboarding. The customer's explanation that the re-routing was necessary due to logistical constraints was noted, but the reviewing analyst remained concerned about the lack of transparency in the supply chain.

The relationship history was further complicated by the discovery of a counterparty address in a comprehensively sanctioned jurisdiction. While the payments themselves were not directed to the sanctioned jurisdiction, the association of a counterparty with that jurisdiction elevated the risk profile of the account. The reviewing analyst initiated a review of the bank's screening processes to determine why this association was not identified earlier. The customer's exposure to a sanctioned jurisdiction, even indirectly, represents a significant deviation from the expected activity profile and raises questions about the adequacy of the customer's own compliance controls.

The customer's transactional behavior was also compared to other businesses in the same sector. Eastbrook Distribution Partners LP and Saltmarsh Distribution Partners LP, both operating in the wholesale distribution sector, exhibited transaction profiles that were markedly different from Obsidian Produce Corp. Their activity was primarily domestic, with international wires limited to documented seasonal sourcing, aligning with their expected profiles. The stark contrast between Obsidian Produce Corp. and these comparable businesses further highlighted the anomalous nature of the subject's account activity. The reviewing analyst concluded that Obsidian Produce Corp.'s transactional behavior was not representative of a typical wholesale agricultural commodities business.

The relationship manager documented ongoing challenges in obtaining timely and comprehensive responses from Obsidian Produce Corp. regarding transaction inquiries. Requests for supporting documentation were frequently met with delays, and the information provided was often incomplete or contradictory. The customer's reluctance to provide clarity regarding the intermediate owner holding exactly forty-nine percent also contributed to the overall assessment of the relationship. The reviewing analyst noted that this ownership structure, combined with the observed transactional behavior and the lack of transparency, presented significant challenges in maintaining a comprehensive understanding of the customer's risk profile.

The review of the relationship history indicates a significant divergence between the expected activity profile recorded at onboarding and the observed transactional behavior. The high volume of international wires, the involvement of counterparties with unclear connections to the declared business model, and the use of a transshipment hub all suggest a more complex and potentially higher-risk operation than initially anticipated. The customer's inability to substantiate the business purpose for these activities, combined with the discovery of a counterparty address in a sanctioned jurisdiction, underscores the need for a thorough reassessment of the relationship and the associated risks. The reviewing analyst concluded that the customer's account activity was not commensurate with the medium risk tier assigned at onboarding.

## Account Profile and Baseline Activity

Account 47-68844-3 was opened on behalf of Marblehead Capital Group LLC on August 21, 2023. The relationship manager’s initial customer profile indicated the entity was formed in Delaware as a holding company for a portfolio of commercial real estate investments in the Mid-Atlantic region. The stated source of wealth for the beneficial owners was commercial property management and leasing. The account was established with a low six-figure initial deposit, which the customer represented as operating capital transferred from an account held at another domestic financial institution. The anticipated activity profile projected moderate monthly transaction volumes, consisting primarily of incoming rent payments and outgoing disbursements for property maintenance, taxes, and debt service. The expected payment methods included automated clearing house credits and debits, domestic wire transfers, and occasional check deposits.

During the first several months following account opening, the transaction activity within the Marblehead Capital Group LLC account appeared broadly consistent with the stated business purpose and the initial projections. The monitoring system established a statistical baseline reflecting regular monthly credit inflows totaling several thousand dollars, primarily originating from a small group of domestic entities, which the relationship manager noted were consistent with commercial tenants. Debit activity during this initial phase consisted of routine payments to local service providers, tax authorities, and what appeared to be debt service payments to another domestic financial institution. The volume of wire transfer activity was low, and the counterparties were exclusively domestic. The account maintained an average monthly balance in the low six-figure range, and the overall transaction patterns did not trigger any automated alerts or manual reviews during this period. The established baseline indicated a predictable cycle of rent collection and operational disbursements, with no significant deviations or unexplained spikes in volume.

The initial review of the account’s historical activity confirmed that the early transaction patterns aligned with the profile of a domestic commercial real estate holding company. The counterparties involved in the incoming automated clearing house credits were consistent with the entities listed on the rent rolls provided by the customer during the onboarding process. The outgoing payments were directed to recognizable vendors providing services typical for property management, such as landscaping, janitorial services, and utilities. The frequency and magnitude of the transactions remained within the parameters established by the monitoring system's baseline, and no significant anomalies or unexpected counterparties were identified during this initial phase. ## Channel, Device, and Session Analytics

A review of digital access logs associated with the Cortex Bank and Trust account held by Obsidian Produce Corp. (account 32-19231-2) was conducted to evaluate the technical circumstances surrounding the transaction activity observed during the review period. The analysis focused on authentication events, session origins, device characteristics, and profile modifications. The objective of this review was to determine whether the digital footprint associated with the account access aligned with the stated business operations of the customer or indicated potential unauthorized access, evasion tactics, or coordination with the other subjects of this investigation.

The digital access records for Obsidian Produce Corp. over the review period demonstrated a consistent pattern of logins originating from a specific geographic location. The primary internet protocol address associated with successful authentication events resolved to a commercial internet service provider located in a jurisdiction known as a major global transshipment hub. This location is not consistent with the customer's registered business address or the geographic footprint described during account onboarding. While the use of a remote location for account access is not inherently indicative of illicit activity, the concentration of logins from a transshipment hub is notable given the red flags observed in the broader case, specifically the re-routing of shipping documents through similar jurisdictions.

Further examination of the session data revealed that the device used for the majority of these logins presented a consistent digital fingerprint. The device characteristics, including the operating system version, browser type, and screen resolution, remained stable across multiple sessions throughout the review period. This consistency suggests that the account was likely accessed by a single user or a small group of users utilizing the same hardware, rather than being subject to widespread credential compromise or automated bot activity. The absence of significant variations in the device fingerprint over time supports the conclusion that the access, while originating from an unexpected location, was likely conducted by an authorized individual or an entity acting on behalf of Obsidian Produce Corp.

A review of the session timing indicated that the account access occurred during hours that align with the business day in the transshipment hub jurisdiction, rather than the business hours of the customer's registered location. This temporal pattern further corroborates the geolocation data and suggests that the entity managing the account operations may be physically located in or operating in coordination with entities in the transshipment hub. The correlation between the login times and the business hours of the remote location is consistent with an arrangement where account management has been delegated to a third party or where the primary operator of the account is based outside the customer's stated jurisdiction.

An analysis of authentication events identified several instances of failed login attempts preceding successful access. These failed attempts typically involved incorrect password entries and occurred in clusters. However, the subsequent successful logins originated from the same internet protocol address and utilized the same device fingerprint as the established pattern. This suggests that the failed attempts were likely the result of user error rather than an organized brute-force attack or credential stuffing campaign. The system did not register any account lockouts or security alerts triggered by excessive failed login attempts, indicating that the authentication process, despite the errors, remained within typical operational parameters.

During the review period, specifically in late August 2023, a review of the account profile modifications revealed a change to the primary contact email address associated with Obsidian Produce Corp. This change occurred on August 24, 2023. The new email address utilized a generic, web-based provider and did not incorporate the corporate domain previously associated with the account. Following this modification, the account experienced a period of heightened transactional activity, including the initiation of funds transfers that were subsequently held for sanctions screening review. The proximity of the profile change to the suspicious activity is a common indicator in cases involving account takeover or the deliberate obfuscation of communication channels.

The digital access logs were also reviewed for evidence of coordinated activity with the other subjects of this report, Greystone Management Trading Co. and Marblehead Capital Group LLC. The analysis did not identify any shared internet protocol addresses, device fingerprints, or overlapping session times between the Obsidian Produce Corp. account and the accounts held by the other subjects. The absence of shared digital infrastructure suggests that, while the entities may be connected through transactional relationships or common counterparties, they are likely operating independently from a technical perspective. The digital evidence does not support a conclusion that the accounts are being managed by a single operator or through a centralized infrastructure.

A specific review of the session data surrounding the transaction involving the payment blocked and reported, which totaled $656,822.37, revealed that the login session during which this payment was initiated originated from the established internet protocol address in the transshipment hub. The device fingerprint matched the historical pattern, and the authentication process did not register any anomalies. This suggests that the initiation of the blocked payment was conducted by the same entity that had been consistently accessing the account throughout the review period. The digital evidence surrounding this specific transaction does not indicate unauthorized access or the involvement of an unknown third party at the technical level.

Similarly, the session data associated with the second payment held pending resolution of the name match, amounting to $444,469.39, followed the established pattern. The login occurred from the transshipment hub jurisdiction, utilizing the known device fingerprint. The consistency of the digital footprint across these significant transactions further reinforces the assessment that the account access was conducted by the primary operator, despite the geographic discrepancy with the customer's stated location.

The analysis of the digital evidence supports the finding that the Obsidian Produce Corp. account was consistently accessed from a jurisdiction known as a transshipment hub, utilizing a stable device fingerprint. The session timing aligned with the business hours of the remote location. While profile modifications were observed prior to significant transactional activity, the overall digital footprint did not indicate widespread credential compromise or an organized cyberattack. The evidence also ruled out shared digital infrastructure with the other subjects of this investigation. The geographic origin of the account access, combined with the red flags observed in the shipping documents, remains a central factor in the evaluation of the customer's activity.

## Adverse Media and Public Record Research

A review of public records and adverse media was conducted for Marblehead Capital Group LLC. A search of the corporate registry in the jurisdiction of formation indicated that Marblehead Capital Group LLC was registered on August 11, 2023. The registry filings identify two managing members, neither of whom were identified as subjects or counterparties in this review. A search of the corporate registry for the identified managing members yielded no additional affiliations. The registry filings indicate that the principal place of business for Marblehead Capital Group LLC is a commercial address shared with several other entities. This address was not identified in the account opening documentation or transaction records for the subject.

Research was conducted to identify any civil litigation involving Marblehead Capital Group LLC. A search of state and federal court dockets yielded no confirmed matches. A search of county-level civil dockets in the jurisdiction of formation returned one possible match. This possible match involved a breach of contract claim filed on September 13, 2023. The plaintiff in this claim was a commercial real estate holding company, and the defendant was an entity with a name highly similar to the subject, but operating in a different state. The reviewing analyst was unable to confirm this match, as the court filings did not contain sufficient identifying information, such as an exact address or principal names, to definitively link the defendant to Marblehead Capital Group LLC. Given the lack of corroborating details and the geographic disparity, this possible match was not considered a significant risk indicator.

A review of public records for liens and judgments was performed. A search of state-level Uniform Commercial Code filings returned no results for Marblehead Capital Group LLC. A search of county clerk records in the jurisdiction of formation returned a notice of federal tax lien filed against an entity with a similar name. The reviewing analyst compared the address on the lien notice with the address on file for the subject. The address on the lien notice was a residential address located in a different county, and no connection could be established between this address and Marblehead Capital Group LLC. The reviewing analyst determined that this was a false positive match.

Research was conducted to identify any regulatory actions involving Marblehead Capital Group LLC. A search of the Securities and Exchange Commission's EDGAR database and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission's disciplinary history database yielded no results. A search of the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority's BrokerCheck system also yielded no results. The reviewing analyst searched the databases of state-level financial regulators in the jurisdiction of formation and the jurisdiction where the subject maintains its primary business address. No regulatory actions or enforcement proceedings were identified.

A comprehensive adverse media search was conducted using commercial databases and open-source search engines. The search strings included the name of the subject, its principals as identified in the corporate registry, and variations of its address. The search yielded no confirmed adverse media related to Marblehead Capital Group LLC.

During the adverse media review, the reviewing analyst identified a news article published on September 18, 2023, regarding a regulatory investigation into a logistics company operating under a similar name in a foreign jurisdiction. The article alleged that the foreign logistics company was involved in facilitating the circumvention of export controls. The reviewing analyst assessed this article to determine if the foreign entity was related to the subject. The foreign entity operated in a different industry sector and was located in a jurisdiction with no known connection to Marblehead Capital Group LLC. Furthermore, the names of the principals associated with the foreign entity, as reported in the article, did not match any individuals associated with the subject. Based on these factors, the reviewing analyst concluded that the foreign logistics company mentioned in the article was not related to Marblehead Capital Group LLC.

A further adverse media search returned an article published on September 19, 2023, detailing a civil lawsuit involving an investment firm with a name that shared the first word of the subject's name. The lawsuit alleged misrepresentation of investment returns. The reviewing analyst cross-referenced the details provided in the article with the known information regarding Marblehead Capital Group LLC. The investment firm mentioned in the article was headquartered in a different state and its principals, as named in the article, were not the managing members identified in the corporate registry filings for the subject. The reviewing analyst determined that this article was a false positive match.

The adverse media search also identified a press release dated September 25, 2023, issued by a non-governmental organization, detailing a report on environmental violations by a mining company. The mining company's name was partially similar to the subject's name. The reviewing analyst noted that the mining company operated in a completely different industry and geographic region than Marblehead Capital Group LLC. The reviewing analyst concluded that this press release did not pertain to the subject.

In summary, the public record and adverse media research yielded no confirmed derogatory information regarding Marblehead Capital Group LLC. The corporate registry filings confirmed the entity's formation date of August 11, 2023, and identified its managing members. No civil litigation, liens, judgments, or regulatory actions were confirmed against the subject. Several possible matches identified during the research were investigated and subsequently determined to be false positives based on discrepancies in geographic location, industry sector, or principal names. The lack of confirmed adverse information does not mitigate the risks identified in the transactional review, but it provides context regarding the subject's public profile during the review period.

## Interview Summary

An interview was conducted with the relationship manager assigned to the Greystone Management Trading Co. account to discuss the transactions flagged during the review period. The relationship manager indicated that Greystone Management Trading Co. operates as a general trading company, facilitating the import and export of various goods, though they were unable to provide a precise list of commodities typically handled. When questioned about the specific payments held for review, the relationship manager stated that they believed the transactions were related to routine trading activities. They recalled a brief conversation with a representative of Greystone Management Trading Co. in late August 2023, during which the customer mentioned expanding their operations to include new international suppliers. The relationship manager could not recall the specific names of these new suppliers or the countries involved, noting only that the customer had described the expansion as a significant opportunity.

The relationship manager was asked about the customer’s onboarding process and whether any specific due diligence had been performed regarding potential exposure to sanctioned jurisdictions. They confirmed that standard onboarding procedures were followed, which included screening the entity name and the names of its principal owners against the relevant sanctions lists. The relationship manager noted that no matches were identified at the time of account opening. When presented with the information that a counterparty address associated with a recent transaction was located in a comprehensively sanctioned jurisdiction, the relationship manager expressed surprise. They stated that they were not aware of any business dealings by Greystone Management Trading Co. involving that specific jurisdiction and reiterated that the customer had not disclosed any such connections during their recent discussions.

Further questioning regarding the relationship manager's understanding of the customer's supply chain revealed a lack of detailed knowledge. The relationship manager acknowledged that they had not reviewed the shipping documents associated with the flagged transactions. When informed that the shipping documents appeared to have been re-routed through a known transshipment hub, the relationship manager suggested that this might be a common practice in the logistics industry to optimize shipping routes, though they conceded they had no specific expertise in international shipping logistics. They could not provide any documentary evidence or customer statements to substantiate this explanation for the routing. The relationship manager also stated they were unaware of the significance of the intermediate owner holding exactly forty-nine percent, a detail that had been identified during the enhanced due diligence review.

An interview was also conducted with the branch manager at the location where the Greystone Management Trading Co. account was originally opened. The branch manager recalled the initial onboarding of the customer, noting that the account was opened by a representative who presented standard corporate documentation. The branch manager stated that the representative described the business as a trading company focused on domestic distribution, with plans to eventually expand internationally. The branch manager did not recall any mention of specific international markets or counterparties during the initial account opening process. They confirmed that the standard know-your-customer information was collected and that the initial account activity was consistent with the anticipated volume and type of transactions.

When asked about recent interactions with the customer, the branch manager indicated that branch staff had minimal contact with Greystone Management Trading Co. representatives in recent months. They noted that the majority of the customer’s transactions were conducted electronically, primarily through wire transfers and ACH payments. The branch manager was unaware of the specific transactions that had been flagged for sanctions review. Upon being informed of the payment references stripped of originator detail, the branch manager stated that they had not observed this pattern in the customer’s earlier transaction history. They suggested that this might be an issue with the customer’s payment processing software or a change in their internal procedures, but could not offer a definitive explanation.

A telephone interview was subsequently conducted with the designated point of contact for Greystone Management Trading Co. The customer representative was asked to provide context for the transactions flagged during the review period, specifically the payment blocked and reported in the amount of $656,822.37. The representative stated that the payment was for a shipment of industrial materials sourced from a new supplier. When asked for the name and location of this supplier, the representative provided the name of a company located in a non-sanctioned jurisdiction, contradicting the information derived from the counterparty address identified during the investigation. The representative claimed that the materials were essential for a large contract they had recently secured but declined to provide a copy of the contract or specific details about the end-user.

The customer representative was then questioned about a second payment held pending resolution of the name match, totaling $444,469.39. The representative explained that this payment was related to a separate shipment of goods from a different supplier. They were asked to explain why the shipping documents for this transaction appeared to have been re-routed through a transshipment hub. The representative stated that this routing was arranged by the supplier's logistics provider and that they were not involved in determining the specific shipping route. They maintained that the use of transshipment hubs was a standard practice to reduce shipping costs and transit times. When pressed for documentation to support this assertion, the representative stated that they would need to request the information from their supplier and could not provide it immediately.

The customer representative was also asked about the ownership structure of Greystone Management Trading Co., specifically regarding the intermediate owner holding exactly forty-nine percent. The representative stated that this structure was established for tax and liability purposes and was a common arrangement in their industry. They denied any knowledge that this ownership structure might be used to obscure ultimate beneficial ownership or circumvent sanctions regulations. When questioned about the payment references stripped of originator detail, the representative claimed that this was an administrative error caused by a recent update to their accounting software. They stated that they were working to resolve the issue and ensure that future payments included complete originator information. The representative’s explanations for the flagged activity were noted, but they were unable to provide sufficient documentary evidence during the interview to fully substantiate their claims or definitively resolve the sanctions concerns raised by the transaction patterns.

## Key Finding

The reviewing analyst established that the ultimate beneficiary of the funds transfer was not the stated counterparty, Tidewater Logistics Trading Co., but rather an individual previously identified as a politically exposed person. Examination of the Swift messaging revealed that on June 4, 2024, instructions were amended to direct the funds to account 76-55389-9. Further inquiry into the beneficiary details for this account confirmed the holder to be Desmond Ravensworth. This individual's profile aligns with the risk factors identified during the initial screening of the transaction, which involved an intermediate owner holding exactly forty-nine percent. The sum directed to this account was $265,816.90. This finding indicates that the payment instructions were deliberately altered to bypass sanctions screening controls, routing funds intended for a sanctioned entity through an intermediary account. The transaction was subsequently blocked, and the matter escalated for further review.

## Remediation and Account Restriction Actions

Upon completion of the review into the activities of Greystone Management Trading Co., maintaining Cortex Bank and Trust account 77-26136-1, a series of remediation and restriction measures were implemented. The initial action involved the immediate placement of a hold on a pending payment directed to Tidewater Logistics Trading Co., a transaction flagged during routine OFAC screening due to a potential name match. This payment, valued at $444,469.39, was held pending a comprehensive review of the underlying trade documentation and the resolution of the screening alert. The reviewing analyst noted that the shipping documents associated with this transaction indicated that the goods were re-routed through a transshipment hub, a factor that elevated the risk profile of the transaction and necessitated further scrutiny.

Simultaneously, a broader review of the account activity was initiated, focusing on transactions involving counterparties that exhibited characteristics consistent with heightened sanctions risk. This review encompassed the period from August 11, 2023, through June 14, 2024. The aggregate value of the screened transactions under review during this period was $640,768.29. A significant portion of this activity involved payments to and from entities where the payment references appeared to have been stripped of originator detail, a practice that obscured the true nature and origin of the funds. This observation, combined with the presence of counterparty addresses in comprehensively sanctioned jurisdictions, prompted the bank to escalate the review and implement enhanced monitoring protocols.

As a result of these findings, a formal restriction was placed on the Greystone Management Trading Co. account, limiting its ability to initiate outgoing wire transfers, particularly international wires. This restriction was deemed necessary to mitigate the risk of further exposure to potentially sanctioned parties or jurisdictions. The relationship manager was instructed to communicate this restriction to the customer and request additional information regarding the nature of their business relationships with Tidewater Logistics Trading Co., Silverthorn Fabrication Inc., Eastbrook Distribution Partners LP, Saltmarsh Distribution Partners LP, and Ironwood Trading Inc. The customer was asked to provide a detailed explanation for the use of transshipment hubs and to substantiate the legitimate business purpose of the transactions where originator details were missing.

In addition to the wire transfer restriction, the bank implemented a rule requiring manual review of all incoming funds transfers to the Greystone Management Trading Co. account. This measure was designed to ensure that any funds received from the identified counterparties or other potentially high-risk entities were subjected to enhanced scrutiny before being credited to the account. The reviewing analyst was tasked with monitoring the account activity closely and escalating any transactions that appeared to deviate from the customer's stated business profile or that exhibited further red flags, such as intermediate ownership structures holding exactly forty-nine percent, a common tactic used to circumvent sanctions regulations.

The remediation process also involved a thorough review of the bank's screening systems and procedures. The investigation revealed that the initial screening mechanisms had failed to identify the potential sanctions risks associated with certain transactions, highlighting a need for system calibration and enhanced training for personnel responsible for reviewing screening alerts. The bank initiated a project to update its screening algorithms and improve the accuracy of its name-matching capabilities. Furthermore, a targeted training program was developed for staff involved in trade finance and cross-border payments, emphasizing the importance of identifying and escalating red flags associated with sanctions evasion, such as the re-routing of goods and the use of complex ownership structures.

A separate payment, valued at $656,822.37, which had been previously blocked and reported to the relevant authorities, remained frozen in accordance with regulatory requirements. The declared value of the shipment named in the trade documents associated with this blocked payment was $504,014.65. The discrepancy between the payment amount and the declared value of the goods was noted as a further area of concern, although the primary reason for the blockage was the identified sanctions nexus. The bank continued to cooperate with the authorities regarding this blocked transaction and maintained the hold on the funds.

Given the severity of the findings and the customer's inability to provide satisfactory explanations for the observed red flags, the bank initiated a formal relationship review process for Greystone Management Trading Co. The review committee was convened to evaluate the overall risk posed by the customer and to determine the appropriate course of action, which could include the eventual closure of the account. The committee considered the aggregate value of the screened transactions, the presence of counterparty addresses in sanctioned jurisdictions, and the apparent attempts to obscure originator details. The committee also took into account the customer's responsiveness to requests for information and their willingness to cooperate with the bank's enhanced due diligence efforts.

Pending the outcome of the relationship review, the restrictions on the Greystone Management Trading Co. account remained in place. The bank committed to ongoing enhanced monitoring of the account, with a specific focus on identifying any attempts to circumvent the imposed restrictions or to engage in further activity that could indicate exposure to sanctioned parties. The reviewing analyst was directed to maintain a detailed log of all account activity and to report any suspicious or unusual transactions to the Financial Intelligence Unit for further investigation. This ongoing monitoring was considered essential to mitigate the bank's risk and to ensure compliance with all applicable sanctions regulations. The case was categorized as a medium risk tier, reflecting the complexity of the observed activity and the potential regulatory implications.

## Law Enforcement Coordination and Information Sharing

On August 18, 2023, Cortex Bank and Trust received an administrative subpoena from an external law enforcement agency. The subpoena sought records pertaining to Obsidian Produce Corp. and requested account opening documents, signature cards, and transactional histories for account 32-19231-2. The request covered the period from August 11, 2023, through the date of the subpoena's receipt. Cortex Bank and Trust complied with the request, providing the requested documentation within the specified timeframe. The subpoena referenced an ongoing investigation but did not provide specific details regarding the nature of the inquiry. The reviewing analyst noted the subpoena's receipt in the case file but could not determine the exact scope or focus of the external agency's investigation based on the information provided in the request.

Following the receipt of the subpoena, the reviewing analyst initiated a review of Obsidian Produce Corp.’s account activity within the timeframe specified by the external agency. This review identified several transactions involving Silverthorn Fabrication Inc. and Ironwood Trading Inc. The analyst observed that a payment held pending resolution of a name match, amounting to $444,469.39, was associated with Ironwood Trading Inc. The payment instructions lacked specific originator details, which was identified as a potential attempt to obscure the source of the funds. The reviewing analyst documented these findings in the case file.

On August 21, 2023, Cortex Bank and Trust initiated a 314(b) information sharing request with the institution holding the account for Silverthorn Fabrication Inc. The request sought information regarding the nature of the business relationship between Obsidian Produce Corp. and Silverthorn Fabrication Inc., as well as any relevant transactional history that might clarify the purpose of the funds transfers observed. The request was based on the observation that the payment references associated with these transfers appeared to be stripped of originator detail, a pattern consistent with attempts to obscure the origin of funds. The request aimed to gather additional context to assist in evaluating the potential risk associated with the observed activity.

The responding institution provided a response on August 24, 2023. The response indicated that Silverthorn Fabrication Inc. maintained an active business account and that the transactions with Obsidian Produce Corp. were ostensibly related to the procurement of specialized equipment. However, the responding institution also noted that Silverthorn Fabrication Inc. had recently initiated transactions involving entities located in jurisdictions known for transshipment activities. The response did not provide further specifics regarding these transshipment activities but confirmed that the transactions with Obsidian Produce Corp. were part of a broader pattern of international trade.

The reviewing analyst incorporated the information received from the 314(b) request into the ongoing investigation. The information suggested a potential connection between the transactions involving Obsidian Produce Corp. and broader international trade activities, potentially involving transshipment hubs. The analyst noted that the shipping documents associated with some of the transactions under review appeared to have been re-routed through a known transshipment hub. This observation, combined with the information received from the 314(b) request, suggested a potential risk of exposure to sanctioned jurisdictions or entities.

On August 28, 2023, Cortex Bank and Trust received a follow-up inquiry from the external law enforcement agency that had issued the initial subpoena. The inquiry requested further clarification regarding specific transactions identified in the records previously provided. The reviewing analyst reviewed the requested transactions and provided the external agency with the available information, including the details obtained through the 314(b) information sharing process. The analyst also provided the external agency with documentation related to a second payment held pending resolution of a name match, which was associated with Ironwood Trading Inc. and amounted to $444,469.39.

The reviewing analyst continued to monitor the activity in Obsidian Produce Corp.’s account. On September 13, 2023, the analyst observed a transaction involving Eastbrook Distribution Partners LP. The transaction details indicated that Eastbrook Distribution Partners LP was involved in the distribution of goods related to the transactions previously identified. The analyst noted that Eastbrook Distribution Partners LP had an intermediate owner holding exactly forty-nine percent, a structure sometimes used to obscure ultimate beneficial ownership and potentially evade sanctions screening thresholds. The analyst documented this observation in the case file.

On September 18, 2023, Cortex Bank and Trust initiated a second 314(b) information sharing request, this time with the institution holding the account for Eastbrook Distribution Partners LP. The request sought information regarding the ownership structure of Eastbrook Distribution Partners LP and the nature of its business relationship with Obsidian Produce Corp. The request was prompted by the observation of the forty-nine percent intermediate ownership structure and the potential risk associated with such structures in the context of international trade.

The responding institution provided a response on September 25, 2023. The response confirmed the ownership structure of Eastbrook Distribution Partners LP but did not provide substantial new information regarding the business relationship with Obsidian Produce Corp. The response indicated that Eastbrook Distribution Partners LP was engaged in general distribution activities and that the transactions with Obsidian Produce Corp. were consistent with its stated business purpose. The reviewing analyst documented this response in the case file, noting that the ownership structure remained a potential risk factor despite the responding institution's assessment.

Throughout the review period, the reviewing analyst maintained communication with the external law enforcement agency, providing updates as requested and responding to inquiries regarding specific transactions. The analyst also continued to monitor the account activity for Obsidian Produce Corp., documenting any relevant findings in the case file. The information gathered through the subpoena process, the 314(b) information sharing requests, and the ongoing monitoring of the account activity contributed to the overall assessment of the potential risk associated with Obsidian Produce Corp. and its counterparties. The analyst noted that the aggregate value of the screened transactions under review was $640,768.29. The information sharing and coordination efforts provided additional context for evaluating the observed activity, particularly regarding the potential risks associated with transshipment hubs and obscured beneficial ownership structures.

## Filing Determination

Cortex Bank and Trust is filing this report because the activity described above is consistent with exposure to a sanctioned party or jurisdiction that screening either missed or flagged and the business escalated incorrectly and no legitimate business purpose was identified for it. The determination rests on the key finding recorded above. The relationship has been placed under enhanced monitoring, the monitoring scenarios that generated the underlying alerts have been retuned for this customer segment, and a relationship review has been scheduled. Supporting documentation is retained in internal case file FIU-2024-1728 and is available to law enforcement on request.
