## Transaction Analysis

The activity under review centered on a single outbound wire transfer initiated from the Hearthstone Marine Services Inc. operating account, 41-19402-1. On October 2, 2023, the customer initiated a wire for $2,908,549.43, identifying the beneficiary as Highfield Marine Services Partners LP. The transfer was directed to an account at a large domestic commercial bank. The stated purpose of the wire was settlement of an outstanding invoice for specialized marine equipment. Review of the transaction details and subsequent communication with the customer established that the transfer was induced by a fraudulent email communication.

The transaction analysis focused on the circumstances surrounding the initiation of the wire, the deviation from the customer's historical payment patterns, and the indicators of compromise within the communication channel. The customer, Hearthstone Marine Services Inc., is a commercial marine contractor. Historical account activity indicates a pattern of regular wire transfers to established vendors, typically ranging from a low five-figure sum to a mid six-figure sum. These payments generally settle invoices for materials, equipment leasing, and subcontractor services. The $2,908,549.43 wire on October 2, 2023, represented a significant deviation in both magnitude and beneficiary from this established pattern. It was the largest single outbound transfer recorded on the account since its inception.

The sequence of events leading to the fraudulent transfer began on September 26, 2023. The customer's accounts payable department received an email appearing to originate from Windlass Exports Inc., a known vendor with whom Hearthstone Marine Services Inc. had an existing commercial relationship and an outstanding, legitimate invoice for equipment. The email communication instructed the customer to remit payment for the outstanding invoice to a new bank account, citing an ongoing internal audit and a temporary freeze on their primary operating account.

Analysis of the email communication, provided by the customer during the subsequent investigation, revealed a critical discrepancy. The sender's email domain closely mimicked the legitimate domain of Windlass Exports Inc., differing by only a single character. This lookalike domain was designed to deceive the recipient into believing the communication was authentic. The deceptive nature of the email was further compounded by the inclusion of a fraudulent invoice attached to the message. The invoice mirrored the formatting, branding, and details of legitimate invoices previously issued by Windlass Exports Inc., including the correct outstanding balance amount.

The fraudulent email was received by an accounts payable clerk at Hearthstone Marine Services Inc. Relying on the apparent authenticity of the communication, the clerk updated the vendor's payment instructions in the customer's internal accounting system. On October 2, 2023, the clerk initiated the wire transfer for $2,908,549.43 through Cortex Bank and Trust's commercial online banking platform.

A notable aspect of the transaction initiation was the timing. The wire was entered into the online banking system just minutes before the bank's established daily cutoff time for outgoing wire transfers. This timing is frequently observed in instances of business email compromise, as it limits the window of opportunity for the sending institution to identify anomalies or for the customer to realize the error and request a cancellation before the funds are dispatched.

Furthermore, the communication from the fraudulent actor contained language emphasizing urgency. The email stressed the need for immediate payment to avoid delays in equipment delivery, a tactic designed to pressure the customer into circumventing standard verification procedures. In this instance, the urgency language was successful in overriding the customer's internal dual-approval control for large outgoing wires. The clerk who initiated the transfer bypassed the requirement for a secondary authorization from a senior manager, citing the immediate need expressed in the email.

The beneficiary of the wire transfer, Highfield Marine Services Partners LP, was not the vendor named on the original, legitimate invoice from Windlass Exports Inc. The fraudulent invoice provided in the email directed payment to this unrelated entity. The customer did not recognize Highfield Marine Services Partners LP and had no prior business dealings with them. The discrepancy between the invoicing vendor and the wire beneficiary is a significant indicator of potential fraud, yet it went unnoticed during the initiation process at Hearthstone Marine Services Inc.

The funds were successfully transmitted to the receiving institution on October 2, 2023. The customer became aware of the fraud on October 5, 2023, when a representative from the legitimate Windlass Exports Inc. inquired about the status of the overdue payment. Hearthstone Marine Services Inc. immediately contacted Cortex Bank and Trust to report the unauthorized transfer and request a recall of the funds.

Cortex Bank and Trust initiated a hold harmless request to the receiving institution on October 5, 2023. Subsequent communication with the receiving bank confirmed that a portion of the funds remained in the beneficiary account. The receiving institution was able to freeze $668,966.37. The remaining balance of the wire had already been disbursed from the beneficiary account prior to the receipt of the recall request.

The analysis of the account activity and the circumstances surrounding the wire transfer indicates a sophisticated business email compromise scheme. The fraudulent actor successfully utilized a lookalike domain, fabricated documentation, and urgency tactics to deceive the customer into authorizing a large-dollar transfer to an unintended beneficiary. The transaction deviated significantly from the customer's historical activity profile and bypassed internal controls. The residual loss to the customer, representing the unrecoverable portion of the original wire amount, was $2,239,583.06. The activity is consistent with funds induced out of a customer account by deception and moved by wire.

## Detailed Chronology

The review period commenced on September 20, 2023, when an incoming email was received by Adrian Nakashima at his business address. Bank records indicate that Nakashima, acting in his capacity as an authorised signer for Hearthstone Marine Services Inc., was the primary point of contact for vendor payments. The email, ostensibly from an established vendor, Windlass Exports Inc., contained an invoice for marine equipment parts. A review of the email headers conducted during the investigation revealed that the sender domain differed by a single character from the legitimate domain used by Windlass Exports Inc. in previous correspondence. The email requested payment via wire transfer rather than the customary automated clearing house method used in prior dealings with this vendor. The invoice itself appeared visually consistent with previous invoices from Windlass Exports Inc., but the remittance instructions directed funds to an account held in the name of Obsidian Equipment Holdings Ltd. at an external institution.

On September 26, 2023, a second email from the lookalike domain was received by Nakashima. This communication referenced the invoice sent on September 20, 2023, and included language stressing the urgency of the payment, citing impending supply chain disruptions if the funds were not received promptly. The email explicitly requested that the payment process bypass the standard dual-approval control established by Hearthstone Marine Services Inc. for outbound transfers exceeding a specific threshold. Internal bank records confirm that Nakashima initiated an outbound wire transfer later that day. The transfer, in the amount of $2,908,549.43, was initiated from the Hearthstone Marine Services Inc. account ending in 41-19402-1. The beneficiary of the wire transfer was listed as Obsidian Equipment Holdings Ltd., matching the remittance instructions on the fraudulent invoice. The transfer was initiated minutes before the established daily cutoff time for wire processing at Cortex Bank and Trust. Despite the established dual-approval requirement for transfers of this magnitude, the transaction was processed based on the authorization provided by Nakashima alone, consistent with the urgency language in the fraudulent email.

Following the execution of the wire transfer on September 26, 2023, there was no further communication from the lookalike domain. On October 2, 2023, a representative from the legitimate Windlass Exports Inc. contacted Hearthstone Marine Services Inc. regarding the outstanding invoice. This inquiry prompted an internal review by Hearthstone Marine Services Inc., which led to the discovery of the fraudulent email and the subsequent wire transfer to Obsidian Equipment Holdings Ltd. Cortex Bank and Trust was notified of the suspected fraud on October 3, 2023.

Upon notification, Cortex Bank and Trust immediately initiated a recall request for the wire transfer of $2,908,549.43 sent on September 26, 2023. The receiving institution was contacted, and a hold was placed on the beneficiary account held by Obsidian Equipment Holdings Ltd. On October 4, 2023, the receiving institution confirmed that a portion of the funds remained in the account and had been successfully frozen. The amount frozen at the receiving institution was $668,966.37. The receiving institution indicated that the remainder of the funds had already been disbursed or transferred prior to the receipt of the recall request.

Further investigation into the disposition of the unfrozen funds revealed a complex web of subsequent transfers. While Cortex Bank and Trust does not have direct visibility into the transactions at the external institution, information provided by the receiving institution indicated that a significant portion of the funds was rapidly moved to other entities. On October 5, 2023, the receiving institution reported that transfers had been made from the Obsidian Equipment Holdings Ltd. account to accounts held by Highfield Marine Services Partners LP, Coastal Ridge Management Enterprises LLC, and Granite Point Trading Group LLC. These entities appear to have no established business relationship with Hearthstone Marine Services Inc. or the legitimate Windlass Exports Inc. The rapid dispersion of funds to multiple unrelated entities is consistent with attempts to obfuscate the origin and ultimate destination of the illicit proceeds.

On October 9, 2023, Cortex Bank and Trust received formal confirmation from the receiving institution regarding the status of the recall request. The receiving institution stated that the frozen funds, totaling $668,966.37, would be returned to Cortex Bank and Trust following the completion of their internal review processes. The return of these funds was successfully processed and credited back to the Hearthstone Marine Services Inc. account ending in 41-19402-1 on October 31, 2023. However, the receiving institution confirmed that the remaining funds could not be recovered. The residual loss to the customer, Hearthstone Marine Services Inc., resulting from the fraudulent wire transfer on September 26, 2023, was $2,239,583.06. This figure represents the original wire amount less the funds successfully recovered from the receiving institution.

On November 1, 2023, Cortex Bank and Trust conducted a comprehensive review of the account activity for Hearthstone Marine Services Inc., as well as the accounts held by Ulises Jankowski and Adrian Nakashima. The review focused on identifying any other potentially anomalous or unauthorized transactions during the period leading up to and following the fraudulent wire transfer. The review did not identify any other transactions exhibiting similar red flags or deviations from established account profiles. The activity in the accounts held by Ulises Jankowski and Adrian Nakashima, other than the initiation of the fraudulent wire transfer by Nakashima on September 26, 2023, appeared consistent with historical patterns and stated account purposes. The investigation determined that the loss of $2,239,583.06 was an isolated incident resulting from the sophisticated email compromise and the subsequent circumvention of internal controls by an authorized signer acting under false pretenses. The chronological sequence of events, from the initial receipt of the deceptive email to the partial recovery of funds, highlights the speed with which the fraudulent scheme was executed and the challenges associated with recovering funds once they have been dispersed through multiple intermediary entities.

The introduction of an international beneficiary, particularly involving a substantial sum, materially altered the jurisdictional risk profile of the account.

The investigation determined that the destination of the $2,908,549.43 wire transfer was central to the suspected typology. The funds were directed to a foreign jurisdiction, increasing the difficulty of recovery and the complexity of the investigation. The reviewing analyst noted that the beneficiary institution in London was the intended recipient of the funds induced by deception. The cross-border nature of the transfer exploited the jurisdictional boundaries between the United States and the United Kingdom, complicating efforts to freeze and repatriate the funds.

Following the initiation of the wire transfer on October 4, 2023, efforts were made to recall the funds. The receiving institution in London was contacted, and a portion of the funds was successfully frozen. The amount frozen at the receiving institution was $668,966.37. The recovery of these funds required coordination across international borders, highlighting the jurisdictional challenges inherent in cross-border wire fraud typologies. The location of the frozen funds in a foreign jurisdiction required adherence to international protocols and cooperation with foreign financial intelligence units.

The remainder of the wire transfer, which could not be recovered, resulted in a residual loss to the customer. The residual loss to the customer was $2,239,583.06. The unrecovered funds were presumed to have been further dispersed within the United Kingdom or transferred to other jurisdictions, further compounding the geographic complexity of the case. The reviewing analyst concluded that the use of a foreign beneficiary institution was a deliberate strategy to place the funds beyond the immediate reach of domestic recovery efforts, leveraging jurisdictional boundaries to facilitate the suspected fraud.

The geographic assessment of Jankowski's account activity revealed a transition from localized, domestic transactions to dispersed domestic transfers, culminating in a significant international wire transfer. The transactions involving Highfield Marine Services Partners LP, Coastal Ridge Management Enterprises LLC, and Granite Point Trading Group LLC established a pattern of activity that spanned multiple domestic jurisdictions, inconsistent with the customer's profile. The subsequent attempted transfer of $2,908,549.43 to a beneficiary institution in the United Kingdom represented the highest level of jurisdictional risk observed during the review period. The cross-border nature of this transaction, and the resulting challenges in recovering the full amount, underscored the geographic complexities associated with the suspected typology. The movement of funds from Florida to Washington, Texas, New York, and ultimately the United Kingdom, demonstrated a concerted effort to utilize multiple jurisdictions to obscure the movement and ultimate destination of the funds.

## Channel, Device, and Session Analytics

The initiation of the fraudulent outbound wire transfer from the account of Hearthstone Marine Services Inc. occurred during an authenticated session on the Cortex Bank and Trust corporate banking portal on October 3, 2023. The session was authenticated using the credentials assigned to Ulises Jankowski. A review of digital banking logs for this session revealed that the login occurred at an Internet Protocol address geolocated to an area near the registered address of Hearthstone Marine Services Inc. in the United States. The device fingerprint captured during this session matched the profile of a device previously used by Jankowski to access the portal and authorize routine transactions. No anomalies were detected in the login sequence; multi-factor authentication was satisfied using a one-time passcode delivered to a mobile number long associated with Jankowski's profile.

The absence of irregular login attributes suggests that the credentials were not compromised through a remote brute-force attack or credential stuffing originating from an unfamiliar location. The matching device fingerprint and the successful completion of the multi-factor authentication challenge indicate that the session was likely initiated by Jankowski himself, or by someone with physical access to his trusted device and mobile phone. This technical evidence is inconsistent with a scenario in which an external actor gained unauthorized access to the banking portal from an unknown device or location to initiate the transfer independently.

An analysis of session activity immediately preceding the October 3, 2023 transfer revealed a sequence of events consistent with a user acting under the influence of deceptive instructions. The session commenced shortly before the bank's established daily cutoff time for processing outgoing wire transfers. Within minutes of authentication, a new payee profile was created for Obsidian Equipment Holdings Ltd. The creation of this payee profile was followed almost immediately by the initiation of the wire transfer for $2,908,549.43. The rapid succession of payee creation and transfer initiation, particularly so close to the processing deadline, is an observable pattern in cases where a user has been manipulated by urgent demands, a factor noted elsewhere in the investigation.

The digital logs show no evidence of hesitation or the typical review period often observed when corporate users initiate high-value transfers to new beneficiaries. The sequence was executed swiftly, supporting the assessment that the user was following specific, externally provided instructions rather than conducting independent business activity. Furthermore, the payee name entered during this session, Obsidian Equipment Holdings Ltd., did not correspond to any vendor previously associated with Hearthstone Marine Services Inc., nor did it match the entities typically involved in the customer's legitimate maritime supply chain.

A review of the digital banking activity for Jankowski's credentials in the days leading up to the October 3, 2023 event yielded no evidence of preceding compromise. Between September 20, 2023 and October 2, 2023, logins occurred from recognized IP addresses and devices, and the resulting activity was consistent with routine corporate banking operations, such as reviewing balances and approving domestic payments to established vendors. There were no recorded failed login attempts, password resets, or changes to the multi-factor authentication contact details during this period. The lack of such precursor events further diminishes the likelihood of an account takeover prior to the session in which the fraudulent transfer was initiated.

Following the execution of the October 3, 2023 transfer, no further logins using Jankowski's credentials were recorded until October 4, 2023, when the customer contacted the bank to report the suspected fraud. At that time, access to the corporate portal for all users associated with Hearthstone Marine Services Inc. was suspended pending investigation.

While the session characteristics strongly suggest that Jankowski was the individual operating the portal, the bank's investigation sought to determine how the deceptive instructions were delivered and acted upon. The analysis of the digital banking session itself cannot confirm the source of the manipulation, but the timing and execution of the transfer align with the receipt of fraudulent communication designed to bypass established internal controls. The swift creation of the Obsidian Equipment Holdings Ltd. payee profile and the immediate initiation of the transfer, occurring just prior to the wire cutoff, reflect a scenario where the user was compelled to act quickly, overriding customary verification procedures.

The technical evidence gathered from the digital banking logs supports a conclusion of authorized access resulting in an unauthorized or unintended transfer, rather than a technical compromise of the bank's systems or the customer's credentials by an external party operating independently. The logs indicate that the bank's authentication protocols functioned as designed, and the transaction was executed based on instructions provided during an authenticated session originating from a recognized device and location. The critical failure occurred outside the digital banking environment, where the user was induced to authorize a payment to a fraudulent beneficiary.

The analysis of the session data, therefore, directs the focus of the investigation toward the circumstances surrounding the communication received by the user and the internal control environment of Hearthstone Marine Services Inc., rather than indicating a vulnerability in the bank's digital channels. The technical findings establish that the mechanism of the loss was the manipulation of an authorized user, a pattern characteristic of business email compromise or similar social engineering typologies. The digital footprint provides a clear timeline of the execution but relies on other investigative streams to illuminate the deception that precipitated the $2,908,549.43 transfer.

## Interview Summary

On October 9, 2023, the reviewing analyst interviewed the relationship manager assigned to Hearthstone Marine Services Inc. regarding the events preceding the outbound funds transfer of $2,908,549.43. The relationship manager stated that they were contacted by the customer’s chief financial officer on October 4, 2023, regarding a pending invoice payment to Windlass Exports Inc. According to the relationship manager, the customer indicated that the payment instructions had been updated via email correspondence earlier that day. The customer reportedly forwarded this email chain to the relationship manager. The relationship manager noted that the email, ostensibly from a known contact at Windlass Exports Inc., directed the payment to a new beneficiary, Obsidian Equipment Holdings Ltd. The relationship manager stated that they did not observe the slight variation in the sender’s domain name at the time.

The relationship manager further stated that the customer expressed significant urgency regarding the transfer, citing potential penalties for delayed settlement. The relationship manager recalled that the customer requested an override of Cortex Bank and Trust’s standard dual-approval requirement for commercial wire transfers exceeding a specific threshold. The relationship manager indicated they processed this override based on the customer’s stated urgency and their established relationship with Hearthstone Marine Services Inc. The reviewing analyst noted that the transaction record confirms the wire was initiated on October 4, 2023, shortly before the daily processing cutoff time, consistent with the reported timeline. The relationship manager confirmed they did not independently verify the new payment instructions with Windlass Exports Inc. prior to approving the transfer.

Following the interview with the relationship manager, the reviewing analyst contacted branch staff at the location where the customer's account was primarily serviced. The branch manager confirmed that the relationship manager had discussed the pending wire transfer on the afternoon of October 4, 2023. The branch manager stated that the relationship manager mentioned the customer’s request to bypass the dual-approval control due to an urgent deadline. The branch manager indicated they did not review the supporting documentation or the email correspondence forwarded by the customer, relying instead on the relationship manager’s assessment of the situation. The branch staff interviewed were unable to provide additional context regarding the specific individuals involved at Hearthstone Marine Services Inc. or Windlass Exports Inc.

On October 31, 2023, the reviewing analyst conducted a telephone interview with the chief financial officer of Hearthstone Marine Services Inc. The customer confirmed their intent to pay an outstanding invoice to Windlass Exports Inc. for marine equipment. The customer stated that they received an email on October 4, 2023, which appeared to be from their usual contact at Windlass Exports Inc. The customer indicated this email contained new wire instructions, directing payment to Obsidian Equipment Holdings Ltd. instead of the previously established account for Windlass Exports Inc. The customer acknowledged forwarding this email to the relationship manager and requesting the expedited processing of the wire.

When questioned about the beneficiary name discrepancy, the customer stated they believed Obsidian Equipment Holdings Ltd. was a subsidiary or affiliated entity of Windlass Exports Inc., as suggested in the fraudulent email. The customer confirmed they did not verify this relationship or the new account details through a secondary communication channel, such as a phone call to a known number for Windlass Exports Inc. The customer also acknowledged the urgency expressed in their communication with the relationship manager, attributing it to the approaching payment deadline and the late receipt of the amended instructions.

The customer further stated that they only became aware of the suspected fraud on October 5, 2023, when they contacted Windlass Exports Inc. regarding a separate matter and were informed that payment had not been received. The customer confirmed they immediately notified Cortex Bank and Trust upon realizing the deception. The reviewing analyst noted that the customer’s account aligns with the sequence of events recorded by the bank, including the initiation of the wire transfer and the subsequent notification of suspected fraud. The customer was unable to provide further information regarding Obsidian Equipment Holdings Ltd. or the individuals behind the fraudulent email domain.

The reviewing analyst compared the accounts provided by the relationship manager, branch staff, and the customer. The narrative provided by all parties is consistent regarding the receipt of the email with new payment instructions, the communication between the customer and the relationship manager, and the urgent processing of the wire transfer. The accounts diverge slightly concerning the level of scrutiny applied to the documentation. The relationship manager acknowledged reviewing the forwarded email but failing to identify the lookalike domain, while the branch manager confirmed they did not review the materials at all. The customer admitted to accepting the new instructions without secondary verification, relying on the apparent authenticity of the email.

The interview findings corroborate the transactional data, confirming that the transfer of $2,908,549.43 was initiated based on fraudulent instructions received via a compromised or spoofed communication channel. The interviews highlight the effectiveness of the deception, which successfully leveraged urgency to bypass established security controls and induce the customer to authorize a payment to an unintended beneficiary. The information gathered during these interviews supports the assessment that the activity is consistent with a business email compromise scheme. The investigation into the recovery of the funds and the identification of the individuals associated with the beneficiary account is detailed in subsequent sections of this report. The customer confirmed they had no prior business relationship with Obsidian Equipment Holdings Ltd. and could identify no legitimate reason for funds to be directed to that entity. The reviewing analyst noted that the failure to independently verify the amended payment instructions was a critical factor in the successful execution of the suspected fraud.

## Key Finding

Reviewing analysts determined that the funds transfer activity initiated by Hearthstone Marine Services Inc. was inconsistent with the customer's stated business profile and historic transaction patterns. The determinative finding centered on a series of outbound wire transfers. The reviewing analyst established that on June 21, 2024, a total of $2,306,290.85 was remitted to an external account held by Falcon Crest Marine Services Trading Co. at a foreign financial institution. This entity was not identified as a known vendor or counterparty during the customer onboarding process, and the customer was unable to substantiate a legitimate business purpose for the transfers. The funds were routed through Cortex Bank and Trust account 42-22407-9. The activity is consistent with funds induced out of a customer account by deception and moved by wire to a beneficiary the customer never intended to pay.

## Remediation and Account Restriction Actions

Following the identification of the fraudulent outbound wire transfer on October 5, 2023, Cortex Bank and Trust executed immediate containment measures on the account held by Hearthstone Marine Services Inc. The relationship manager initiated a total freeze on all outbound electronic funds transfers from account 41-19402-1, encompassing wire transfers, automated clearing house debits, and external account transfers. This restriction was implemented to prevent further capital flight while the investigation into the $2,908,549.43 disbursement proceeded. Concurrently, a stop payment order was applied to all pending, unpresented checks drawn on the account. The bank’s fraud operations unit contacted the receiving institution to request a recall of the funds; however, this request was only partially successful, resulting in the recovery of $668,966.37. The remaining balance of the transfer, totaling $2,239,583.06, represents the final loss sustained by the customer.

The reviewing analyst determined that the existing dual-approval control framework on the customer’s online banking profile had been compromised. The investigation revealed that the urgency language embedded within the fraudulent communication had successfully induced the customer's authorized signers to bypass standard verification protocols. Consequently, the bank deactivated the online wire origination capability for Hearthstone Marine Services Inc. Any future wire transfer requests must now be submitted in person at a branch location, supported by physical documentation, and subject to enhanced authentication procedures by a branch manager. The automated clearing house origination limit was also reduced to zero, effectively disabling the customer's ability to initiate such transactions electronically. 

In addition to transactional restrictions, the bank initiated a comprehensive review of the Hearthstone Marine Services Inc. relationship. This review scrutinized the customer’s internal control environment, focusing on their procedures for vendor verification, invoice approval, and the management of payment instructions. The bank requested that the customer provide an attestation detailing the remediation steps taken to secure their email infrastructure and prevent future occurrences of business email compromise. The customer was required to demonstrate the implementation of multi-factor authentication for all email access and the deployment of advanced threat protection software capable of detecting lookalike domains, such as the one utilized in this incident. 

Given the magnitude of the loss and the identified vulnerabilities in the customer's payment authorization process, the relationship was escalated to the bank’s high-risk customer review committee on October 31, 2023. The committee evaluated the customer's remediation efforts and the residual risk posed to Cortex Bank and Trust. The committee concluded that while the customer had taken substantial steps to address the immediate security failures, the relationship warranted ongoing enhanced due diligence. The bank determined that the account relationship would be maintained, subject to strict adherence to the newly implemented channel limitations and the successful completion of periodic risk assessments.

The Financial Intelligence Unit applied targeted monitoring rules to the Hearthstone Marine Services Inc. profile. These rules are designed to flag any future transaction requests that exhibit characteristics similar to the fraudulent event. Specifically, the system is configured to alert on any wire transfer request that involves a beneficiary name discrepancy, a change in payment instructions for an established vendor, or an origination request submitted shortly before the daily processing cutoff. Furthermore, the monitoring rules will monitor for any attempts to circumvent the in-branch origination requirement or any unusual patterns of automated clearing house activity that might indicate an attempt to utilize alternative payment channels.

The accounts held by Ulises Jankowski and Adrian Nakashima, identified as subjects during the investigation, were also subjected to enhanced scrutiny. Although no direct complicity in the fraudulent event was established, their roles as authorized signers on the Hearthstone Marine Services Inc. account necessitated a review of their individual account activities. The reviewing analyst placed a temporary hold on external transfers from accounts 55-71902-2 and 56-32620-3 pending a thorough analysis of their transactional history. No suspicious activity was identified in these personal accounts, and the holds were subsequently released on November 1, 2023. However, both accounts remain subject to elevated monitoring thresholds.

The bank also conducted a secondary review of relationships associated with the counterparties identified during the investigation, including Windlass Exports Inc., Obsidian Equipment Holdings Ltd., Highfield Marine Services Partners LP, Coastal Ridge Management Enterprises LLC, and Granite Point Trading Group LLC. The purpose of this review was to ascertain if these entities had been targeted by similar fraudulent schemes or if they exhibited any indicia of involvement in the movement of the illicit funds. The review did not yield any evidence to suggest that these entities were complicit or had been victimized in a similar manner. 

Following the submission of this Suspicious Activity Report, Cortex Bank and Trust commits to a ninety-day review cycle for the Hearthstone Marine Services Inc. relationship. This review will assess the customer’s compliance with the mandated security protocols and evaluate the effectiveness of the bank’s implemented controls. The Financial Intelligence Unit will continue to monitor the account for any deviation from expected transactional behavior and will initiate a continuing activity report if further suspicious activity is identified. The bank will also maintain communication with law enforcement agencies regarding the ongoing efforts to recover the outstanding funds and will provide any additional information requested to support their investigation. The restrictions placed on the customer's online banking profile will remain in effect indefinitely, pending a formal reassessment of the customer's risk profile and the demonstrated efficacy of their internal controls over an extended period.

## Law Enforcement Coordination and Information Sharing

Following the identification of the suspected wire fraud activity involving the outbound transfer of $2,908,549.43, Cortex Bank and Trust initiated coordination efforts with relevant law enforcement agencies and other financial institutions. On November 1, 2023, the Financial Intelligence Unit received a grand jury subpoena issued by the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York. The subpoena requested all account records, transaction histories, wire transfer details, and know-your-customer documentation pertaining to Ulises Jankowski and account 55-71902-2, covering the period from September 20, 2023, through the date of the request. The subpoena specifically referenced an ongoing investigation into business email compromise and associated money laundering schemes. Cortex Bank and Trust complied with this subpoena, providing the requested documentation on November 15, 2023, through established secure electronic transmission channels. The provided records included the wire transfer authorization form, customer profile information, and correspondence between Ulises Jankowski and the relationship manager regarding the execution of the transfer.

In addition to the grand jury subpoena, the Financial Intelligence Unit received a written request for information from the Federal Bureau of Investigation on December 5, 2023. This request, while not compelling the production of documents, sought supplementary details regarding the circumstances surrounding the initiation of the $2,908,549.43 wire transfer. The request focused on the communication channels used by Ulises Jankowski to instruct the relationship manager, specifically inquiring about any anomalies noted in the email instructions or subsequent phone confirmations. The reviewing analyst provided a detailed response on December 12, 2023, outlining the sequence of events, including the receipt of the email with the lookalike sender domain and the urgency language employed by the sender to bypass the standard dual-approval control. The response also highlighted the discrepancy between the beneficiary name on the wire instructions and the name of the invoicing vendor, Obsidian Equipment Holdings Ltd., as well as the timing of the transfer initiation, which occurred just prior to the daily wire cutoff.

Concurrent with the law enforcement coordination, Cortex Bank and Trust engaged in information sharing under Section 314(b) of the USA PATRIOT Act. On November 8, 2023, the Financial Intelligence Unit initiated a 314(b) request to the receiving institution of the $2,908,549.43 wire transfer. The request sought information regarding the beneficiary account, the identity of the account holder, and any subsequent movement of funds following the receipt of the wire. The receiving institution responded on November 14, 2023, confirming that the beneficiary account was held in the name of a recently established limited liability company with no prior relationship with the receiving institution. The response also indicated that a portion of the funds had been rapidly dissipated through a series of outbound wire transfers to various domestic and international accounts shortly after the initial deposit.

Furthermore, the receiving institution disclosed that they had placed a freeze on the remaining balance in the beneficiary account upon receiving a hold harmless request from Cortex Bank and Trust, which had been transmitted on October 31, 2023, immediately following the discovery of the suspected fraud. The receiving institution confirmed that $668,966.37 had been successfully frozen and remained in the beneficiary account pending further investigation and potential recovery efforts. This information was critical in determining the residual loss to the customer, which was calculated to be $2,239,583.06. The details obtained through the 314(b) information sharing process were subsequently incorporated into the ongoing internal investigation and shared with law enforcement in accordance with the provisions of the USA PATRIOT Act.

On January 18, 2024, the Financial Intelligence Unit initiated a second 314(b) request, this time directed to a different financial institution where Ulises Jankowski was known to maintain accounts. This request aimed to ascertain if similar patterns of activity or suspicious transactions had been observed in those accounts, particularly concerning interactions with entities such as Windlass Exports Inc., Highfield Marine Services Partners LP, Coastal Ridge Management Enterprises LLC, or Granite Point Trading Group LLC. The responding institution, on January 25, 2024, provided a summary of activity indicating that while Ulises Jankowski held accounts there, no transactions resembling the suspected wire fraud scheme or involving the aforementioned counterparties had been detected during the review period. They did note, however, a series of moderate cash deposits that appeared inconsistent with his stated occupation, though these were deemed unrelated to the specific typology under investigation by Cortex Bank and Trust.

Throughout the review period, Cortex Bank and Trust maintained ongoing communication with the Federal Bureau of Investigation, providing updates on the status of the internal investigation and any new information uncovered. This included sharing the findings from the 314(b) requests and the details regarding the lookalike domain and the urgency language used in the email instructions. The bank also facilitated an interview between the relationship manager and investigators from the Federal Bureau of Investigation on February 15, 2024. During this interview, the relationship manager recounted the interactions with Ulises Jankowski on October 4, 2023, and October 5, 2023, detailing the pressure exerted to expedite the wire transfer and the failure to recognize the discrepancy in the beneficiary name. The relationship manager also provided context regarding the typical communication patterns with Ulises Jankowski prior to the incident.

The coordination efforts extended to the filing of a Suspicious Activity Report, which detailed the suspected wire fraud, the individuals and entities involved, and the red flags identified during the investigation. The report included a comprehensive narrative describing the sequence of events, the methods employed to induce the transfer, and the subsequent movement of funds. The information obtained through law enforcement requests and 314(b) information sharing was integrated into the narrative to provide a complete picture of the activity. Cortex Bank and Trust continued to monitor the accounts of Ulises Jankowski and the related entities throughout the remainder of the review period, remaining responsive to any further inquiries or requests for information from law enforcement agencies or other financial institutions. The bank's actions demonstrated a commitment to full cooperation in the investigation of the suspected fraudulent activity and the pursuit of any available avenues for recovery of the misappropriated funds.

## Filing Determination

Cortex Bank and Trust is filing this report because the activity described above is consistent with funds induced out of a customer account by deception and moved by wire to a beneficiary the customer never intended to pay and no legitimate business purpose was identified for it. The determination rests on the key finding recorded above. The relationship has been placed under enhanced monitoring, the monitoring scenarios that generated the underlying alerts have been retuned for this customer segment, and a relationship review has been scheduled. Supporting documentation is retained in internal case file FIU-2024-1732 and is available to law enforcement on request.
